# Auto-generated content → git merge drivers (don't hand-resolve machine churn)

> **Principle.** A file region that is **deterministically (re)generated from the tree** must never be hand-resolved on merge/rebase. Two parallel branches mutate the same generated region → git's default 3-way text merge reports a conflict on pure machine churn. The fix is a `.gitattributes` merge driver matched to the region's *shape*, codified at the root — never a per-occurrence manual resolution (a recurring gate is a fix, not a chore → `KB § PATTERNS/common/methodology-execution-discipline.md`).

## Three shapes, three drivers

| Generated shape | Conflict cause | Correct driver | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Append-only log** (`project-history/*.ndjson` — vector-costs, auto-improvement, absorptions, branch-tree) | each branch appends DISTINCT lines to the tail | built-in **`merge=union`** | keeps BOTH sides' lines, no markers — appends never conflict. Codified 2026-05-30. |
| **Derived block** (`<!-- kb-counts:start:X -->…:end:X -->` inventory tables in `02-LANDSCAPE.md` / `06-AGENTS.md` / `AGENT-CONTEXT.md`) | each branch bumps the SAME row/grand-total (file & line tallies) | custom **`merge=kb-counts`** → `scripts/hooks/merge-kb-counts.sh` | `union` is WRONG (duplicates table rows). Instead **re-derive** the block from the merged tree. Codified 2026-06-05. |
| **Insert-at-anchor entry list** (`LGPD-WARNINGS.md` — `lgpd_flag` always inserts at the top) | every parallel flag inserts at the SAME anchor → always conflicts, and a hand-resolution once silently dropped an unresolved entry (2026-10-10) | custom **`merge=lgpd-warnings`** → `scripts/hooks/merge-lgpd-warnings.sh` → pure `lgpd.merge_warnings` | `union` mangles multi-line blocks; merge BY ENTRY IDENTITY (concern+path): keep every addition, conflict only a block both sides changed differently. Deletes are policed by keeper `check_lgpd_entry_removal`, not by the driver. → `KB § PATTERNS/common/lgpd-entry-keeper.md`. |
| **Hand-numbered tail-appended list + sorted map** (`gate-alignment-inventory.json` — `decisions[]` ids are the next `D<n>`, `gates` gains a row per gate) | every parallel branch appends at the SAME tail and mints the SAME next id → conflict plus possible duplicate ids (s1 `gate-inventory/decision-id-collision`, D18..D21 on 2026-11-07) | custom **`merge=gate-inventory`** → `scripts/hooks/merge-gate-inventory.sh` → pure `gate_alignment.merge_inventory` | `gates` = union (same key edited differently on both sides conflicts); `decisions` = ours + theirs' new entries, renumbered past max on id collision, identical / same gate+decision dropped; output byte-stable (sorted, `indent=1`). Tests: `test_gate_inventory_merge_driver.py`. |

**The discriminator:** is the conflicting region *accumulated* (append) or *recomputed* (derive)? Union for the first; regenerate for the second.

## The regenerating driver (derived blocks)

`scripts/hooks/merge-kb-counts.sh` (git invokes `driver %O %A %B %P`):

0. **3-way merge first:** `git merge-file -p %A %O %B > <merged>`. git does **not** pre-merge for a custom driver — `%A` is only *ours*. Until 2026-11-05 the driver rendered `%A` alone and reported success, which **silently discarded the other side's prose edits** to these docs: in a rebase *ours* is the upstream, so a branch's roster-row rename in `02-LANDSCAPE.md` vanished on every rebase (nosnolimiar, twice), and a queue composition could drop a peer's edit the same way;
1. run `cli.py --render-kb-counts %P --source <merged> --out <scratch>` → regenerates the `kb-counts` blocks belonging to `%P` deterministically from the tree, rewriting **the merged content** (the churn, and any conflict markers that sat *between* the start/end markers). Nothing tracked is written;
2. **marker guard** — if `<<<<<<<`/`=======`/`>>>>>>>` remain (a genuine PROSE edit conflict *outside* the blocks), write the render **with its markers** into `%A` and **exit 1** so git surfaces the real conflict; else copy the render into `%A` and exit 0. **Every conflict exit writes a 3-way merge into `%A`**, because git takes `%A` as the RESULT and a non-zero exit only flags the path. Leaving `%A` as "ours" produced a conflicted file with no markers and the other side's lines silently gone (2026-11-10: dev's `agent-creator` row vanished from 06-AGENTS.md). The render-failure and no-`%P` exits hand back the plain 3-way merge for the same reason.

Counts-only churn → silently correct. Real prose conflict → still surfaced. The safety hinge: the renderer only rewrites the **delimited block**, never the whole file (`mcp/noctusai/tools/kb_sync.py`).

### 🔴 The driver writes `%A` and nothing else — this is load-bearing

The first implementation regenerated by copying `%A` over the **real path**, running `--update-kb-counts` (which rewrites *every* `kb-counts` doc in the tree, not just the merged one), then copying back. That leaves the working tree modified as a side effect.

A single `git merge` hides it completely: git overwrites the working tree from `%A` immediately afterwards. **A `git rebase` cannot survive it.** The sequencer applies one commit per pick; the counts written during pick N reflect the *intermediate* tree, so pick N+1 aborts with `Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge`, and `git rebase --continue` reschedules the same pick — the todo list grows on every attempt and the rebase never finishes. Observed 2026-08-17 replaying 10 commits over `dev` (stalled at 7/10, indefinitely).

The tempting fix is to neutralise the driver for the duration (`-c merge.kb-counts.driver=true`) or to merge instead of rebase. Both are workarounds around a defect *in the driver*, and the second one trips `check_prod_exposure_consent` the moment `dev` carries a consent record. The fix is `--render-kb-counts`: a **pure** CLI mode that reads a source file, regenerates the blocks from the tree, and writes only to the `--out` path the caller owns.

Two details that matter if you touch this:

- **The render goes to a file, never stdout.** `cli.py` prints a banner (and a `--worktree-path` override notice) to stdout before dispatch; piping the render would embed that in a KB doc. `--out` makes the driver immune to any present or future stdout noise.
- **Failure degrades to surfacing the conflict**, never to a half-written doc: if python/the CLI is missing or the render exits non-zero, the driver falls through with the *unrendered* merge result, which still carries its markers and therefore still exits 1.

Regression tests: `mcp/noctusai/tests/test_kb_sync.py::test_render_kb_counts_*` — purity (the on-disk file is byte-identical after a render), block-only rewriting, and that a prose conflict outside the block survives so the marker guard can fire. The shell half — what git actually invokes — is pinned by `mcp/noctusai/tests/test_merge_kb_counts_driver.py`: it runs the real driver in a throwaway repo against a recording stub CLI and asserts the exit-code contract (clean render → 0 + %A rewritten; markers remain / render fails → 1 + %A byte-identical; no %P → 1 without a CLI call), that the other side's non-overlapping prose edit survives (`test_other_sides_prose_edit_survives_the_merge`) and that same-line edits on both sides surface a conflict and that the driver writes %A and nothing else (clean `git status`, no temp leftover).

## Why not `merge=ours` / why not stop stamping

- **`merge=ours` (keep one side)** is unsafe for `02-LANDSCAPE.md` / `CLAUDE.md`: they mix generated blocks with **hand-written prose** → `ours` would silently drop a real concurrent prose edit. The regenerating driver + marker-guard preserves prose conflicts.
- **Stop auto-stamping counts per-commit** would re-open the 2026-06-01 "count regen left dirty → blocks `task_branch` integrate" recurrence, and would also strand the roster-row structural sync the `check_kb_sync` keeper depends on (product-add must update the roster). The driver leaves the per-commit stamp intact and fixes only the *merge* surface.

## Wiring (driver = per-repo git config, NOT committable)

`.gitattributes` (committed) maps the path → driver NAME; the driver body is per-repo git config, registered by **`scripts/hooks/register-merge-drivers.sh [ROOT]`** (idempotent; one `reg` line per driver). Two callers: `scripts/hooks/install-hooks.sh` (developer clones) and `.github/workflows/merge-queue.yml` (the runner — setup-python + `pip install -r mcp/noctusai/requirements.txt` + this script, all before the drain).

A clone that hasn't registered the drivers degrades to the default text merge (the old conflict). Fresh clone: `bash scripts/install-hooks.sh`.

### 🔴 Incident 2026-11-05 — the CI runner never registered them

4 queue entries (core-lead-email-off, julia-mecanismo-v2, agents-optout-paused, julia-content-fixes) were ejected `conflict … 02-LANDSCAPE.md`: every enqueue regenerates the kb-counts blocks, so parallel entries always touch the same block, and on the runner `merge=kb-counts` named an UNDEFINED driver → plain text merge → conflict. The drain's `git merge --no-ff` and `git rebase --onto` both honour drivers once registered (proved in `tests/test_merge_drivers_ci.py`). Keeper `check_merge_drivers_registered_in_ci` now requires: every custom `merge=<name>` in `.gitattributes` is registered by the script, and `merge-queue.yml` invokes it.

`merge-kb-counts.sh` re-renders via `cli.py --render-kb-counts`, which needs the toolkit deps. If python/the CLI/deps are missing it now **exits 1** (a real conflict, stderr says why) instead of keeping stale counts as before. Locally this only bites with a broken venv.

## When you add a new auto-generated surface

1. Decide the shape (append vs derive).
2. Add the `.gitattributes` line (`merge=union` or `merge=<regen-driver>`).
3. Append-only → done (union is built in). Derived → author/extend a regenerating driver + add a `reg` line in `register-merge-drivers.sh` (CI picks it up) + run it now.
4. Codify here + memory; keep `.gitattributes` ↔ `register-merge-drivers.sh` ↔ this doc in sync.

Related: `KB § PATTERNS/common/branching.md` (integrate cleanly) · `KB § PATTERNS/common/methodology-execution-discipline.md` (recurring gate → root fix) · `KB § PATTERNS/architect/noc-graph.md` (committed `graph.json` + merge driver, same family).

## `.merge_file_*` scratch never lands in the primary (2026-11-09)

git creates `.merge_file_XXXXXX` scratch for a custom driver in the **cwd of the process running the merge** — including `git merge-tree --write-tree` trial merges, which run the drivers too. The drivers themselves are fine (they write only `%A` and use the invoking tree's toplevel); the leak was toolkit trial merges (`task_branch landed`/cleanup `_content_on_dev`, `release` cut/manifest) running with the PRIMARY as cwd, so the post-hoc primary guard blamed whichever session ran a Bash call meanwhile. Rules: trial merges run from inside the git dir (`_trial_merge_tree`, `release._default_run_local`), never the primary; the guard (`is_git_merge_scratch`) never attributes the scratch to a session and logs one `git_merge_scratch_ignored` row to `~/.noctus/primary-guard-events.ndjson`; `noctus.dev.mole sweep` removes stale ones (>10 min).

## The merge-driver contract (2026-11-10) — one test, every driver

**Incident.** `git merge origin/dev` into `feat/assistant-chatbot` silently dropped dev's `` - **`agent-creator`** … `` line from `06-AGENTS.md`: the file showed `UU` with **no markers**. `merge-kb-counts.sh` had exited 1 on a real prose conflict but left `%A` as "ours" — git takes `%A` as the merge RESULT, and a non-zero exit only flags the path. Two sibling drivers (`lgpd-warnings`, `gate-inventory`) carried the same flaw on their failure/conflict exits, because each test pinned only its own driver's behaviour.

**The contract** every custom driver honours, on EVERY conflict or failure exit:

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| i | real conflict → exit ≠ 0 **and** `%A` holds conflict markers with **both** sides' lines |
| ii | clean merge → exit 0, the other side's lines present, no markers |
| iii | the driver writes `%A` and nothing else (no tracked file, no scratch leftover) |
| iv | render/toolkit failure → still hand git the plain 3-way merge (`git merge-file -p`), never "ours" alone |

`mcp/noctusai/tests/test_merge_driver_contract.py` pins it through REAL `git merge`. Drivers are **discovered** from `.gitattributes` (`merge=<name>`, builtin `union` excluded) and `register-merge-drivers.sh` (`reg <name> … <script>`), so a new driver is covered the moment it is registered; one with no `SPECS` fixture **fails** the suite — adding a driver means adding its minimal valid base/ours/theirs there (the construction leg). Keeper `check_merge_drivers_have_contract_coverage` (`--check-merge-drivers-have-contract-coverage`, pre-commit, warn-first) is the commit-time backstop.

`merge=union` audit (2026-11-10): applied only to `project-history/*.ndjson` (append-only logs; `ledger.ndjson` is deduped-by-slug-keep-latest on read). A row edited in place on both sides would duplicate, which readers tolerate; no file with structure (JSON/markdown) uses union.

## Merge-loss detector (shadow) — judge the RESULT, not the driver

The contract pins the drivers we know. `noctus.dev.merge_loss_check` (`cli.py --check-merge-loss [--merge-sha SHA] [--no-log]`) judges what actually landed, so it also catches a driver nobody has written yet or a hand resolution.

**Design.** Given a merge (MERGE_HEAD at pre-commit time — the result is the **index** — or a merge commit SHA): base = `merge-base`; for every file changed on BOTH sides, take the zero-context hunks base→ours and base→theirs; every non-trivial **added** line (blank / table-rule / punctuation-only lines are ignored) absent from the result is reported `{path, side, line, base_region}`, **unless** the other side removed the base region that hunk replaced (a legitimate either/or) or removed the lines on both sides of an insertion point. Exempt, and reported under `skipped` (never silent): `project-history/**` (ledgers rewritten in place + tables regenerated from them — the only false-alarm class in the first 25-merge sample), lines inside `kb-counts` generated blocks (re-derived by design), a WHOLE file rendered from a source (a `> Generated from \`<src>\` by \`<cmd>\`` header in ours, theirs AND the result — positional ids such as gate-alignment D-numbers shift on every upstream row; a loss is judged at the source file; benign class found on the 2026-11-10 D2b merge), a still-conflicted index entry, binary/deleted files. Verdicts: `clean` | `dropped` | `unmeasurable` (not a merge / base unreadable — never green, never red). Blind spots: presence not position (a line kept elsewhere counts as kept), a duplicate-count drop is invisible, renames are compared by path.

**Wired in SHADOW (warn + log, never blocks):** (1) `scripts/hooks/pre-commit` step 12b when MERGE_HEAD exists; (2) `merge_queue.py` `Queue.compose` after every `--no-ff` merge entry — the verdict line `[merge-loss] …` lands in the drain log (the runner is ephemeral, so `--no-log`; grep the drain log).

**Telemetry.** Every local run appends `{ts, merge_sha, files, dropped_count, mode:"shadow", verdict}` to `project-history/merge-loss-detector.ndjson` (ledger store; `merge=union`); a run with `dropped_count>0` also files an `auto_improvement_log` `kind=finding`. Each finding is triaged into **Learnings** below.

**Promotion to blocking** — all of: ≥ 20 shadow runs **on real merges** recorded in the ledger; **0 unexplained false alarms** (every flagged merge triaged and written under Learnings as true-positive or a named benign class with its exemption/fix); the benign classes found are either exempted in code with a regression test or documented as unfixable-by-design with a human-ack escape (`Merge-Loss-Reviewed: <file> — <reason>` trailer, to be built then). Until then the owner/steward reads the findings; nothing blocks.
